newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Richina Pacific unfazed by Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Richina Pacific unfazed by Deng's death.

text.p: New Zealand group Richina Pacific said on Thursday that its investment plans in China would not be affected by the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

Richard Yan, Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of Richina Group Ltd, a parent company which owns 51 percent of Richina Pacific, said the signs pointed to a reasonably smooth transition of power, and Deng's death would not impact materially on the country's economy or its political future.
"I think his visions are well understood by all Chinese people and I don't think the course he has created and has gone down the path of will in any way be reversed," Yan said.

"I think the whole thing is going to be treated in a very low-key way...the transitions pretty much have happened in the last two years, and it certainly wouldn't change in any way our views on what we will do in China," Yan said.

Richina Pacific currently has about NZ$40 million invested in China and employs 400-500 people. Its 100 percent-owned Underwater World theme park, currently under construction in Beijing, is expected to open in the third quarter of 1997.
The company also has a 51 percent stake in Shanghai Richina Leather Corporation, which Yan described as probably the largest tannery in China.
Yan said Richina Pacific is looking to grow both its leather and theme park businesses.

"Although we have an aquarium in Beijing, we have been looking at other sites, both in China and in Asia. We are becoming more confident of China in terms of the overall environment, but we do need to do a better job of managing our own businesses with our people," he said.

Yan said revenue from Richina Pacific's China operations had not been publicly projected, as it was subject to the precise timing of the aquarium's opening and how fast the company could ramp up production at the Shanghai tannery.
Yan said the national congress in October of China's Communist Party would be a significant event in terms of China's future direction and leadership.

"The speed (at which) that happens and the quality of the people selected to fill those roles will have a far more fundamental impact on the future economic progress as well as political progress of China, than the passing of Deng Xiaoping,"
